subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Editing and Evaluation Phases
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Editing and Evaluation Phases.

hook.text: Before choosing, your brain simplifies options: rounding numbers, ignoring small differences, setting a reference.

buildup.text: Prospect theory has two phases. First, editing: the brain organizes and simplifies the choice.

discovery.text: Second, evaluation: the edited options are compared using the value function and probability weights.

twist.text: The editing phase is where most biases enter. How you frame a problem determines how it gets evaluated.

climax.text: The same gamble, presented differently, gets different edits and different choices. Frame creates preference.

punchline.text: How you see the choice is the choice.

quiz.question: What happens in prospect theory's editing phase?
options: The brain simplifies and organizes options before evaluating
People skip directly to a final choice
